newsitem.title: CONGO: U.N., Mandela to continue Zairean peace initiative.
newsitem.headline: U.N., Mandela to continue Zairean peace initiative.

text.p: United Nations envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said he and South African President Nelson Mandela would discuss Wednesday's collapse of scheduled Zairean peace talks and continue their efforts to avoid a humanitarian disaster.

"We are not going to give up. We will continue to try to avoid another humanitarian tragedy...to try to get the democratic process on track," Sahnoun told a news conference aboard the ship on which the warring Zairean leaders had been scheduled to meet.

The second face-to-face meeting between Mobutu and Kabila, was to have taken place at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT) but was repeatedly postponed amidst confusion about Kabila's whereabouts. It was cancelled when Kabila refused to board a South African ship in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire.
Sahnoun said he and Mandela would talk to Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on Wednesday night and would invite rebel leader Laurent Kabila to join them for talks in South Africa.
"It is a great disappointment for us as mediators. We had worked hard to organise this," a pale and drawn Sahnoun said quietly, before he somberly left immediately after the news conference.
Mandela is expected to address a news conference at about 2100 GMT Wednesday night after meeting with Mobutu.
